title: Rigveda 10.49: Indra's praise of himself
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.49: Indra's praise of himself: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.49 is a hymn of 11 verses addressed to Indra's praise of himself. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 5r-6v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.49.1-3 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 5r
translation.original_text:
1a̱haṁ dā̍ṁ gṛṇa̱te pūrvya̱ṁ vasv a̱ham brahma̍ kṛṇava̱m mahya̱ṁ vardha̍nam | a̱ham bhu̍va̱ṁ yaja̍mānasya codi̱tāya̍jvanaḥ sākṣi̱ viśva̍smi̱n bhare̍ ||
2māṁ dhu̱r indra̱ṁ nāma̍ de̱vatā̍ di̱vaś ca̱ gmaś cā̱pāṁ ca̍ ja̱ntava̍ḥ | a̱haṁ harī̱ vṛṣa̍ṇā̱ vivra̍tā ra̱ghū a̱haṁ vajra̱ṁ śava̍se dhṛ̱ṣṇv ā da̍de ||
3a̱ham atka̍ṁ ka̱vaye̍ śiśnatha̱ṁ hathai̍r a̱haṁ kutsa̍m āvam ā̱bhir ū̱tibhi̍ḥ | a̱haṁ śuṣṇa̍sya̱ śnathi̍tā̱ vadha̍r yama̱ṁ na yo ra̱ra ārya̱ṁ nāma̱ dasya̍ve ||
translation.text:
1I HAVE enriched the singer with surpassing wealth; I have allowed the holy hymn to strengthen me. I, furtherer of him who offers sacrifice, have conquered in each fight the men who worship not.
2The People of the heavens, the waters, and the earth have stablished me among the Gods with Indra's name. I took unto myself the two swift vigorous Bays that speed on divers paths, and the fierce bolt for strength.
3With deadly blows I smote Atka for Kavi's sake; I guarded Kutsa well with these saving helps. As Ṣushṇa's slayer I brandished the dart of death: I gave not up the Aryan name to Dasyu foes.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 5r (OPenn image 4, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.48.11 ‹-vasūnāṁ rudriyāṇāṁ devo devānāṁ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 5v, begins in RV 10.49.4 ‹-piteva vetasūm̐r abhiṣṭaye tugraṁ›. Verses 10.49.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.49.4-6 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 5v
translation.original_text:
4a̱ham pi̱teva̍ veta̱sūm̐r a̱bhiṣṭa̍ye̱ tugra̱ṁ kutsā̍ya̱ smadi̍bhaṁ ca randhayam | a̱ham bhu̍va̱ṁ yaja̍mānasya rā̱jani̱ pra yad bhare̱ tuja̍ye̱ na pri̱yādhṛṣe̍ ||
5a̱haṁ ra̍ndhaya̱m mṛga̍yaṁ śru̱tarva̍ṇe̱ yan māji̍hīta va̱yunā̍ ca̱nānu̱ṣak | a̱haṁ ve̱śaṁ na̱mram ā̱yave̍ 'karam a̱haṁ savyā̍ya̱ paḍgṛ̍bhim arandhayam ||
6a̱haṁ sa yo nava̍vāstvam bṛ̱hadra̍tha̱ṁ saṁ vṛ̱treva̱ dāsa̍ṁ vṛtra̱hāru̍jam | yad va̱rdhaya̍ntam pra̱thaya̍ntam ānu̱ṣag dū̱re pā̱re raja̍so roca̱nāka̍ram ||
translation.text:
4Smadibha, Tugra, and the Vetasus I gave as prey to Kutsa, father-like, to succour him. I was a worthy King to rule the worshipper, when I gave Tuji dear inviolable gifts.
5I gave up Mr̥igaya to Ṣrutarvan as his prey because he ever followed me and kept my laws. For Âyu's sake I caused Veta to bend and bow, and into Savya's hand delivered Paḍgr̥ibhi.
6I, I crushed Navavâstva of the lofty car, the Dâsa, as the Vr̥itra-slayer kills the fiends; When straightway on the region's farthest edge I brought the God who makes the lights to broaden and increase.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 5v (OPenn image 5, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.49.4 ‹-piteva vetasūm̐r abhiṣṭaye tugraṁ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 6r, begins in RV 10.49.7 ‹-dāsaṁ kṛtvyaṁ hathaiḥ›. Verses 10.49.4-6 end on this page; 10.49.4 begins on fol. 5r.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.49.7-10 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 6r
translation.original_text:
7a̱haṁ sūrya̍sya̱ pari̍ yāmy ā̱śubhi̱ḥ praita̱śebhi̱r vaha̍māna̱ oja̍sā | yan mā̍ sā̱vo manu̍ṣa̱ āha̍ ni̱rṇija̱ ṛdha̍k kṛṣe̱ dāsa̱ṁ kṛtvya̱ṁ hathai̍ḥ ||
8a̱haṁ sa̍pta̱hā nahu̍ṣo̱ nahu̍ṣṭara̱ḥ prāśrā̍vaya̱ṁ śava̍sā tu̱rvaśa̱ṁ yadu̍m | a̱haṁ ny a1̱̍nyaṁ saha̍sā̱ saha̍s kara̱ṁ nava̱ vrādha̍to nava̱tiṁ ca̍ vakṣayam ||
9a̱haṁ sa̱pta sra̱vato̍ dhāraya̱ṁ vṛṣā̍ dravi̱tnva̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāṁ sī̱rā adhi̍ | a̱ham arṇā̍ṁsi̱ vi ti̍rāmi su̱kratu̍r yu̱dhā vi̍da̱m mana̍ve gā̱tum i̱ṣṭaye̍ ||
10a̱haṁ tad ā̍su dhāraya̱ṁ yad ā̍su̱ na de̱vaś ca̱na tvaṣṭādhā̍raya̱d ruśa̍t | spā̱rhaṁ gavā̱m ūdha̍ḥsu va̱kṣaṇā̱sv ā madho̱r madhu̱ śvātrya̱ṁ soma̍m ā̱śira̍m ||
translation.text:
7I travel round about borne onward in my might by the fleet-footed dappled Horses of the Sun. When man's libation calls me to the robe of state I soon repel the powerful Dasyu with my blows.
8Stronger am I than Nabus, I who slew the seven: I glorified with might Yadu and Turvaga. I brought another low, with strength I bent his strength: I let the mighty nine-and-ninety wax in power.
9Bull over all the streams that flow along the earth, I took the Seven Rivers as mine own domain. I, gifted with great wisdom, spread the floods abroad: by war I found for man the way to high success.
10I set within these cows the white milk which no God, not even Tvashṭar's self, had there deposited,– Much-longed-for, in the breasts, the udders of the kine, the savoury sweets of meath, the milk and Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 6r (OPenn image 5, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.49.7 ‹-dāsaṁ kṛtvyaṁ hathaiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 6v, begins in RV 10.49.11 ‹-satyarādhāḥ›. Verses 10.49.7-10 end on this page; 10.49.7 begins on fol. 5v.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.49.11 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 1, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 6v
translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>e̱vā de̱vām̐ indro̍ vivye̱ nṝn pra cyau̱tnena̍ ma̱ghavā̍ sa̱tyarā̍dhāḥ | viśvet tā te̍ harivaḥ śacīvo̱ 'bhi tu̱rāsa̍ḥ svayaśo gṛṇanti ||
translation.text: <sup>11</sup>Even thus hath Indra Maghavan, truly bounteous, sped Gods and men with mighty operation. The pious glorify all these thine exploits, Lord of Bay Coursers, Strong, and Selfresplendent.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 6v (OPenn image 6, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.49.11 ‹-satyarādhāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 7r, begins in RV 10.50.4 ‹-viśveṣu savaneṣu yajñiyaḥ›. Verse 10.49.11 ends on this page; 10.49.11 begins on fol. 6r.
